newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong democracy group abandons mock election.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong democracy group abandons mock election.

text.p: A Hong Kong democracy movement said on Friday it had abandoned a plan to stage a mock election that would have overshadowed Beijing's closed-door moves to pick a leader for the territory after Britain withdraws in 1997.
The Frontier, led by pro-democracy legislators known for their vocal criticism of Beijing, said it lacked the money and time to organise such a polling exercise.

"It is already September and we do not have the time to run a proper election," said Emily Lau, outspoken legislator and the Frontier spokeswoman. "We have also estimated the whole campaign would cost us about HK$1 million, which we do not have."
The future Chief Executive, who will replace departing colonial Governor Chris Patten next July 1, will be appointed by a 400-member China-controlled Selection Committee in November.
A separate shadow election staged by the territory's largest pro-democracy political party, the Democrats, started this week. The result will be announced by early October.

Pro-democracy groups intend to use the mock election concept as an exercise in civic education and to highlight the closed-door process that China is using to appoint Hong Kong's future leader and political establishment.
